typeof gensym
# §1  macro definer + unquote — operands arrive as code, spliced at the call site.
def twice (macro [[e] [ quote [ unquote e add unquote e ] ]])  twice 5
def unless (macro [[c body] [ quote [ if unquote c [0] unquote body ] ]])  unless false [42]
def unless (macro [[c body] [ quote [ if unquote c [0] unquote body ] ]])  unless true [42]
# §2  splice — flatten a list operand into the surrounding sequence.
def callit (macro [[f xs] [ quote [ unquote f splice xs ] ]])  def add3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer][Integer][a add b add c]]  callit add3 [1 2 3]
# §3  manual hygiene via gensym — an introduced binder does NOT capture a same-named user var.
def myor (macro [[a b] [ def g (gensym)  quote [ def unquote g unquote a  if unquote g [unquote g] [unquote b] ] ]])  def tmp 42  myor false tmp
column3: gensym temp doesn't capture the user's tmp

column1: def myor2 (macro [[a b] [ quote [ def tmp unquote a  if tmp [tmp] [unquote b] ] ]])  def tmp 42  myor2 false tmp
column3: UNHYGIENIC: literal tmp captures the user's tmp (the bug gensym fixes)

column1: # §6  Expansion cache (1e) — repeated calls with the same operands reuse the
#     expansion; correctness is unchanged (a hit re-splices identical code).
def inc1 (macro [[a] [ quote [ unquote a add 1 ] ]])  [(inc1 4) (inc1 4) (inc1 9)]
# §7  macroexpand is recursive (macroexpand-all): a macro whose expansion calls
#     another macro is expanded too. A runaway recursive macro errors loudly.
def inner (macro [[x] [quote [unquote x add 1]]])  def outer (macro [[y] [quote [inner unquote y]]])  macroexpand (outer 5)
def loopy (macro [[a] [quote [loopy unquote a]]])  macroexpand (loopy 1)
column3: recursive macro is caught, not looped
